questions.question: List the five levels of the waste hierarchy in order and give an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Avoid and reduce: buy products with less packaging, avoid single-use straws and bags. Reuse: refill bottles, reuse jars and shopping bags, repair items. Recycle: process paper, cans, glass and PET into new products. Recover: compost organic waste or capture landfill gas to generate electricity. Dispose: send remaining waste to a properly managed landfill.

questions.question: Describe how a materials recovery facility separates steel cans, aluminium cans, paper and plastics, and explain why paper can only be recycled a few times while glass can be recycled indefinitely.
questions.expected_answer: Hand sorting removes large items and contaminants; rotating screens separate by size and shape; magnets remove steel cans; an eddy current separator flicks out non-magnetic aluminium cans; air blowers separate light paper; optical sensors identify plastic types and air jets sort them. Paper is recycled by pulping, which shortens and weakens its cellulose fibres each time, so after about five to seven cycles they are too short to make paper. Glass is melted back into molten glass with the same properties, so it can be remade into new glass again and again.

questions.question: Name three types of household hazardous waste, explain how each should be disposed of, and describe three consequences of poor waste management.
questions.expected_answer: Batteries: take to battery drop-off points at shops or municipal sites. Energy-saving bulbs (mercury): take to bulb or hazardous waste drop-off points. Old medicines: return to a pharmacy. Paint, oil and pesticides, and electronic waste: municipal hazardous or e-waste drop-off sites. Consequences: illegal dumping attracts rats, flies and mosquitoes that spread disease; waste blocks storm-water drains and causes flooding; waste washes into rivers and the sea, harming wildlife; burning waste releases toxic smoke; unlined landfills produce leachate that pollutes groundwater and gas that causes fires and climate change.
